catalog.title: Case planning and approval gate
catalog.goal: Prove that the complete case contract is reviewable and no execution or simplified path can bypass exact-snapshot human approval.
preconditions: No approval exists for the newly generated snapshot.
The active change contains current requirements and acceptance contracts.

steps.action: Generate and inspect the normalized case snapshot.
steps.expected: Cases, steps, assertions, six-domain mappings, runners, and evidence policies are visible and schema-valid.

steps.action: Attempt execution without a matching human approval.
steps.expected: Execution is blocked with an approval blocker bound to the current snapshot.

steps.action: Request light, compact, or simplified verification.
steps.expected: The request is rejected and the full six-domain V2 contract remains required.

assertions.statement: The complete proposed case contract is inspectable before execution.
An absent, stale, service-authored, or hash-mismatched approval blocks execution.
No light, compact, partial-domain, or simplified verification path is accepted.

catalog.title: Managed runtime and runner-oracle boundaries
catalog.goal: Prove locked runtime diagnosis, immutable attempt identity, registered runner boundaries, and deterministic final oracles without fallback.
preconditions: The repository business dependency manifests remain unchanged.

steps.action: Run runtime doctor and inspect installed package and browser identities.
steps.expected: Exact versions, browser readiness, provider status, permissions, and blockers are reported.

steps.action: Execute command and Playwright adapter contract tests with immutable fingerprints.
steps.expected: Attempts bind all required identities and reject changed retry fingerprints.

steps.action: Submit Midscene-only observations without a deterministic oracle.
steps.expected: The reading remains blocked and no alternative runtime or oracle is selected.

assertions.statement: The managed runtime reports locked component and browser status with exact blockers and no fallback.
Run and retry identity is complete and mutation of any retry fingerprint is rejected.
Midscene evidence alone cannot produce PASS without a deterministic or explicitly permitted human oracle.

catalog.title: Evidence integrity, readings, six-domain aggregation, and freshness
catalog.goal: Prove that complete content-addressed evidence produces validated readings and that all six domains, rerun scope, freshness, and gates are fact-derived.
preconditions: The approved case snapshot is available.
The EvidenceStore starts from an empty append-only raw log.

steps.action: Persist evidence and validate identity, path, hash, size, producer, and source bindings.
steps.expected: Valid evidence is accepted and tampered, missing, stale, empty, or forged evidence blocks readings.

steps.action: Derive readings and aggregate all six domains from the validated evidence.
steps.expected: Every case has six terminal domain results and prose or manual green reports cannot override them.

steps.action: Change source fingerprints and compute freshness and rerun scope.
steps.expected: Affected concrete case IDs and reasons are returned, and stale evidence blocks the gate.

assertions.statement: Evidence is append-only, content-addressed, fully identity-bound, rebuildable, and fail-closed on integrity violations.
All six domain and release verdicts are derived from validated readings, including governed not_applicable decisions.
Freshness and rerun scope use immutable fingerprints and identify affected case IDs with reasons.

catalog.title: Failure, repair, retry, retest, regression, and break-loop
catalog.goal: Prove that failures remain immutable while retry, repair, retest, regression, closure, reopen, and no-progress escalation follow distinct governed states.
preconditions: A deterministic case has a captured initial failure.
The failure packet is frozen before any repair begins.

steps.action: Classify the failure and route product or test repair through a standard development task.
steps.expected: The failure packet and source evidence remain immutable and the repair owner is explicit.

steps.action: Exercise identical retry and changed-code retest paths.
steps.expected: Retry success is FLAKY, repaired success is PASS AFTER FIX, and prior failure evidence remains present.

steps.action: Run regression scope and repeat a no-progress failure cycle.
steps.expected: Required regressions control closure and repeated no-progress routes to break-loop governance.

assertions.statement: Failure classification creates an immutable packet and an ownership-correct development repair handoff.
Retry, retest, and regression preserve prior attempts and produce FLAKY or PASS AFTER FIX semantics correctly.
Regression failure reopens the loop and repeated no-progress requires a break-loop decision.

catalog.title: Three-page report center
catalog.goal: Prove that overview, case catalog, and case results pages render one validated model across all states with responsive, accessible, print-safe, escaped evidence presentation.
preconditions: Validated report models exist for green, red, blocked, running, canceled, stale, flaky, and pass-after-fix states.

steps.action: Render all three report pages from the validated report model.
steps.expected: Overview, approved case contract, complete attempt history, evidence, freshness, repair, and release state are visible.

steps.action: Exercise desktop, mobile, keyboard, and print layouts in real browsers.
steps.expected: Navigation, verdicts, tables, links, and controls remain readable, operable, and non-overlapping.

steps.action: Inject markup and provider-secret fixtures and manually alter rendered HTML.
steps.expected: Content is escaped and redacted, shared components remain consistent, and JSON gate truth is unchanged.

assertions.statement: All three report pages expose the required lifecycle, case, result, evidence, repair, and release facts from one model.
Desktop, mobile, keyboard, and print review preserve readable verdict and evidence information without overlap.
Rendering escapes hostile content, redacts secrets, reuses shared components, and never becomes gate authority.

catalog.title: V1-to-V2 migration
catalog.goal: Prove that legacy artifacts migrate through explicit dry-run, backup, validation, receipt, rollback, and fail-closed missing-evidence semantics.
preconditions: A disposable fixture contains representative V1 green, incomplete, and malformed verification artifacts.
No production change is mutated by the fixture run.

steps.action: Run migration dry-run and inspect the source inventory and proposed transformations.
steps.expected: The plan names backup references, validation actions, and rollback instructions before mutation.

steps.action: Migrate fixtures and validate the migration receipt.
steps.expected: Valid source facts are preserved and receipt hashes bind inputs, outputs, validation, and rollback.

steps.action: Migrate a V1 green artifact with missing evidence.
steps.expected: The V2 reading is blocked and never inferred as PASS.

assertions.statement: Migration exposes dry-run inventory, backups, validation, and rollback before mutation.
Migration writes a hash-bound receipt and preserves valid source and failed evidence.
Missing V1 evidence becomes a blocked V2 reading and never a PASS.

catalog.title: Shared Kernel and three-host integration
catalog.goal: Prove one host-neutral kernel owns verdict semantics while thin Codex, Claude Code, and CodeFree-O adapters remain synchronized and drift-detectable.
preconditions: The canonical kernel and immutable host lock are present.
The Claude Code and CodeFree-O sibling repositories are available for read-only compatibility validation.

steps.action: Run the shared fixture corpus through all three host adapters.
steps.expected: Normalized artifacts, blocker IDs, verdicts, runtime behavior, and discovery contracts match.

steps.action: Inspect host adapter architecture and public service boundaries.
steps.expected: Verdict logic stays in the kernel and runners, evidence, failures, and rendering use explicit adapters or services.

steps.action: Mutate a disposable host lock or generated contract fixture.
steps.expected: Cross-host drift detection blocks compatibility and names the mismatched identity.

assertions.statement: Codex, Claude Code, and CodeFree-O produce the same kernel contract results.
Host adapters remain thin and explicit service boundaries own execution and presentation concerns.
Kernel, schema, blocker, fixture, wrapper, or generated artifact drift is detected before release.

catalog.title: Release and archive gate
catalog.goal: Prove that release and transactional archive recompute complete Verification 2.0 truth and fail closed on any missing, stale, tampered, open, incompatible, or simplified input.
preconditions: All approved cases have fresh six-domain readings and generated reports.
Three clean-host installation receipts and migration status are available.

steps.action: Build release and archive gate inputs from the current snapshot, readings, evidence index, runtime, kernel, reports, migration, and host receipts.
steps.expected: Gate identities bind all source facts and produce a deterministic decision.

steps.action: Remove or tamper with each required input in disposable fixtures.
steps.expected: Release and archive block with exact source blockers and cannot trust edited HTML or copied green summaries.

steps.action: Run transactional archive success and rollback fixtures.
steps.expected: Archive occurs only after green proof, preserves failed evidence, and rolls back safely on filesystem or compatibility failure.

assertions.statement: Release and archive decisions bind approved cases, six-domain readings, evidence index, freshness, runtime, kernel, reports, migration, and all hosts.
Any unapproved, incomplete, stale, tampered, open, missing, incompatible, or simplified input blocks release and archive.
Archive is transactional, preserves source and failed evidence, and rolls back safely on failure.
